name: Social Security System

references.title: Republic Act 11199 (Social Security Act of 2018)
references.quote: Read 2026-10-07. s.9(a): compulsory coverage for employees "not over sixty (60) years of age", the age at entry; initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. s.11 ends the employer's contribution only at separation; s.12-B(a) retires a member who has reached sixty and is separated, or who has reached sixty-five. So an employee covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed until sixty-five; from sixty-five nothing is charged. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Owner ruling (2026-10-07): a missing date of birth is treated as under sixty (RA 11199 s.9(a) covers every employee not over sixty, and an unrecorded birth date gives no ground to treat the person as over it). s.8(i): compensation is remuneration for services; separation and retirement payments outside remuneration for services are excluded.

references.title: SSS Circular 2024-006 (business employers)
references.quote: Effective January 2025. Regular SS uses the first PHP20,000 monthly salary credit at 5% employee and 10% employer; excess to PHP35,000 belongs to SSS_MPF. MSC is the monthly salary credit between PHP5,000 and PHP35,000.

references.title: SSS Circular 2024-007 (household employers)
references.quote: Household compensation below PHP5,000 takes nine distinct MSC brackets from PHP1,000 to PHP5,000: PHP1,000 below PHP1,250 and PHP500 brackets to PHP5,000 (round to 500, half up, minimum 1,000). The household employer pays the whole 15% regular SS share and the kasambahay nothing. From PHP5,000 compensation the regular employer/employee split applies; the SSS household-employer page deducts the employee share only "if earning more than P5,000.00".

references.title: Republic Act 10361 (Batas Kasambahay)
references.quote: A domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service; where the domestic worker earns less than PHP5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium/contribution.

references.title: SSS: employees page
references.quote: A foreign employee is covered like any other unless an SSS bilateral social security agreement exempts the person.

references.title: SSS contribution base is the monthly ordinary wage
references.quote: Read 2026-11-04. s.8(f): compensation is all actual remuneration for employment. IRR Rule 12 s.6(iii) lists "[b]onuses (except Christmas bonus)" as compensation. IRR Rule 12 s.6(iii) excludes a Christmas bonus and does not name 13th-month pay. Practical treatment: the monthly salary credit reads the ORDINARY_WAGES checkpoint, so 13th month pay, Christmas bonus, separation and retirement pay and SSS benefits are outside the monthly MSC, as are the ad hoc de minimis classes, which post after ADDITIONAL_WAGES; WTAX puts the 13th month and Christmas bonus in its PHP90,000 pool. On a SEMI_MONTHLY schedule each run charges half of the month its own wages imply, whole for a joiner or leaver with one run that month: `ctx.balances` holds tax-year totals, so the second run cannot read what the first paid.

name: SSS Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP)

references.title: Republic Act 11199 (Social Security Act of 2018)
references.quote: Read 2026-10-07. s.9(a): compulsory coverage for employees "not over sixty (60) years of age", the age at entry; initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. s.11 ends the employer's contribution only at separation; s.12-B(a) retires a member who has reached sixty and is separated, or who has reached sixty-five. So an employee covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed until sixty-five; from sixty-five nothing is charged. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Owner ruling (2026-10-07): a missing date of birth is treated as under sixty (RA 11199 s.9(a) covers every employee not over sixty, and an unrecorded birth date gives no ground to treat the person as over it). The Regular SS result establishes coverage, including the first-liability age test.

references.title: SSS Circular 2024-006 (business employers)
references.quote: Effective January 2025. Only a covered SSS member contributes to the Mandatory Provident Fund on salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer.

references.title: SSS Circular 2024-007 (household employers)
references.quote: Same MPF rule for household employers: salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 at 5% employee and 10% employer.

references.title: Republic Act 10361 (Batas Kasambahay)
references.quote: A domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service; where the domestic worker earns less than PHP5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium/contribution.

references.title: SSS: employees page
references.quote: A foreign employee is covered like any other unless an SSS bilateral social security agreement exempts the person.

references.title: MPF uses the same compensation base as regular SS
references.locator: RA 11199 s.8(f); IRR Rule 12 s.6(iii); SSS Circular 2024-006 II.B.2
references.quote: Read 2026-11-04. The MPF salary credit above PHP20,000 through PHP35,000 is part of the same monthly salary credit and follows the same ordinary-wage base as regular SS.

name: Employees Compensation Programme premium

references.title: Presidential Decree 626 (Employees Compensation) as amended
references.quote: Employer-only EC premium keyed to the SSS monthly salary credit. EC covers compulsory SSS private employees, including continued qualifying coverage after sixty; a first liability after the sixtieth birthday does not create EC cover.

references.title: SSS Employees' Compensation Program
references.quote: ECP coverage page; unchanged law corrected in place.

references.title: SSS Circulars 2024-006 and 2024-007
references.quote: Effective January 2025: EC is PHP10 through MSC PHP14,500 and PHP30 from MSC PHP15,000.

references.title: Republic Act 11199 (Social Security Act of 2018)
references.quote: Read 2026-10-07. s.9(a): compulsory coverage for employees "not over sixty (60) years of age", the age at entry; initial compulsory coverage extends through the 60th birthday. s.11 ends the employer's contribution only at separation; s.12-B(a) retires a member who has reached sixty and is separated, or who has reached sixty-five. So an employee covered before sixty keeps contributing while employed until sixty-five; from sixty-five nothing is charged. The first contribution liability date includes earlier employers and is independent of current registration. Owner ruling (2026-10-07): a missing date of birth is treated as under sixty (RA 11199 s.9(a) covers every employee not over sixty, and an unrecorded birth date gives no ground to treat the person as over it). s.8(i): compensation is remuneration for services; separation pay (Labor Code arts.298-299) and retirement pay (RA 7641) are paid for the ending of service, not for it, and are outside the contribution base.

references.title: Republic Act 10361 (Batas Kasambahay)
references.quote: A domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service; where the domestic worker earns less than PHP5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium/contribution.

references.title: SSS: employees page
references.quote: A foreign employee is covered like any other unless an SSS bilateral social security agreement exempts the person.

references.title: EC premium follows the SSS monthly salary credit
references.quote: Read 2026-11-04. The EC premium is keyed to the SSS monthly salary credit, so it follows the same ORDINARY_WAGES base.

name: PhilHealth

references.title: Republic Act 11223 (Universal Health Care Act)
references.quote: A premium on the monthly basic salary of an employed member.

references.title: PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1)
references.quote: One 5% premium on the monthly basic salary, floor PHP10,000, ceiling PHP100,000, "equally shared between the employee and employer" (§V.B). The circular is silent on an odd centavo; recorded default: the employee half truncates and the employer carries the remainder (a half-centavo premium such as basic 15,819 -> 790.95 gives 395.47 / 395.48). §V.G with RA 10361 s.30: where a domestic worker earns less than PHP5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium. This is the circular PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002 ¶1 and PA2026-0042 name.

references.title: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002
references.quote: Premium 5.0% from January 2025, floor PHP10,000, ceiling PHP100,000; employers use the Monthly Basic Salary, and "those deductions to the employee’s pay occasioned by his/her undertime, tardiness, leave(s) without pay, absences, or other similar circumstances shall also be excluded in this computation". https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2025/PA2025-0002.pdf, read 2026-11-05.

references.title: Republic Act 10361 (Batas Kasambahay)
references.quote: A domestic worker is covered by SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG after at least one month of service; where the domestic worker earns less than PHP5,000 a month the employer pays the whole premium/contribution.

references.title: Republic Act 9679 and HDMF Circular 460
references.quote: Pag-IBIG: 2% of an employee's monthly fund salary (see the HDMF scheme). No premium is charged on a settlement run after the exit month that has no monthly basic.

references.title: PhilHealth Monthly Basic Salary excludes 13th month, bonus, commission, overtime and allowances
references.quote: Read 2026-11-05. MBS is "the fixed basic rate of an employee which shall not include sales commission, overtime pay, allowances, thirteenth month pay, bonuses or other gratuity payments", and pay deductions for undertime, tardiness, leave without pay and absences "shall also be excluded in this computation"; for monthly- and daily-paid employees it follows the Estimated Equivalent Monthly Rate of the DOLE Handbook (2024 ch.1 §E: daily rate × factor ÷ 12). So the premium reads the contract rate, whole for a short month, and never the paid BASIC checkpoint, which unpaid days reduce. BASIC only gates it: a run with no paid basic, such as a settlement after the exit month, charges none. On a SEMI_MONTHLY schedule the month's share splits across the two runs, whole for a joiner or leaver with one run that month.

name: Pag-IBIG Fund (Home Development Mutual Fund)

references.title: Republic Act 9679
references.quote: Monthly Fund Salary is basic salary and other allowances received in the month. Contributions use remuneration actually paid for the employment month, including covered allowances and deducting unpaid absence.

references.title: HDMF Circular 460
references.quote: Dated 15 January 2024; contributions effective February 2024 (official DMW annex pp.2-4). Employee contribution is 1% up to PHP1,500 and 2% above PHP1,500; employer contribution is 2%, with a PHP10,000 compensation ceiling.

references.title: HDMF Circular 274
references.quote: Coverage history (certified ONAR copy). Private initial coverage not over 60 is distinct from continuing membership until compulsory Fund retirement at 65. Non-compulsory termination permits mandatory re-enrolment when coverage resumes; self-paying and voluntary classes have no automatic employer payroll counterpart. Membership facts require a recorded evidence reference; missing registration never establishes exemption.

references.title: Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 9679
references.quote: Read 2026-10-07. s.1(a): membership is mandatory for "all employees who are compulsorily covered by the SSS" (a private employee "not over 60 years old"). s.10: "Any member shall be compulsorily retired under the Fund upon reaching age sixty-five (65)", so nothing is charged from sixty-five, nor from sixty for an employee not covered before it (the SSS derivation). Voluntary membership after that (s.3) is the member's, not payroll.

references.title: Republic Act 10361 (Batas Kasambahay)
references.quote: A domestic worker is covered after at least one month of service; where the monthly Fund Salary is below PHP5,000 the employer pays both shares.

references.title: Pag-IBIG Fund Salary excludes 13th month and bonus
references.quote: Read 2026-11-04. RA 9679 s.4 defines compensation as "basic monthly salary plus mandated cost of living allowance"; s.7 computes contributions on that monthly compensation. Circular 460's Fund Salary is "basic salary and other allowances" — a bonus or 13th-month payment is neither. The ORDINARY_WAGES checkpoint applies. On a SEMI_MONTHLY schedule each run charges half of the month its own wages imply, whole for a joiner or leaver with one run that month: `ctx.balances` holds tax-year totals, so the second run cannot read what the first paid.

name: Taxable regular pay (memo for off-cycle withholding)

references.title: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3): supplementary pay is taxed with the period's regular pay on its column. An off-cycle run has no regular pay of its own, so this row keeps the run's taxable regular pay by month. A memo row: it charges nobody and has no cost subtotal.

name: Withholding Tax on Compensation

references.title: Read 2026-10-31: rice and laundry ceilings apply independently to each calendar month; unused limits do not carry. The dependant medical allowance uses the statutory per-semester alternative (PHP1,500 before 6 January 2026; PHP2,000 from that day), independently for January–June and July–December. The sum of each period’s excess enters the separate PHP90,000 annual 13th-month/other-benefits pool. RR29-2025 s.1(c),(d),(g), https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%2029-2025.pdf; predecessor RR2-98 as amended by RR11-2018/RR4-2025.
National Internal Revenue Code (as amended by RA 10963)
references.quote: Annual table (2023): PHP250,000 0%; 15% to 400,000; 22,500 + 20% to 800,000; 102,500 + 25% to 2,000,000; 402,500 + 30% to 8,000,000; 2,202,500 + 35%. s.25(B): a non-resident alien not engaged in trade or business is taxed 25% final on the entire income (de minimis and the PHP90,000 exclusion not deducted). s.24(A)(2): minimum wage earners exempt.

references.title: Revenue Regulations 11-2018
references.quote: Withholding on compensation. Each period withholds on its own Annex E column; the last pay date of the calendar year and the exit run annualise: the year's taxable compensation, plus a previous employer's (from its Form 2316), less the year's withholding; a negative result is refunded on the payslip. The year-end deficiency is withheld from the last payment of compensation for the year. Exclusions (s.2.78.1(B)): the employee shares of SSS, MPF, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG as charged and union dues ((B)(12)); 13th-month pay, other benefits and de minimis excess to PHP90,000 ((B)(11)); minimum wage earner ((B)(13)): exempt on the statutory minimum wage, holiday, overtime, night-shift and hazard pay when the contract's rate for an 8-hour day is at or below the regional daily floor of the workplace in force on the period's last day; a certified BMBE has no floor. Additional compensation paid to a minimum wage earner, such as commissions, fringe benefits, benefits over PHP90,000 and taxable allowances, is taxed alone (s.2.79(A)): "taxable only on such additional compensation received". Fringe benefits: rank-and-file compensation; for supervisory and managerial staff the FBT scheme's instead.

references.title: Revenue Regulations 11-2018, Annex E (withholding tax tables)
Revenue Regulations 29-2025 amending RR 2-98
references.quote: De minimis ceilings: rice PHP2,500 and laundry PHP400 a month, dependants' medical PHP2,000 a semester, uniform PHP8,000, medical assistance, awards and CBA PHP12,000, gifts PHP6,000, 12 days' monetised leave, overtime/night meal 30% of the regional minimum wage a day.

references.title: Soriano v. Secretary of Finance
references.quote: A minimum wage earner is taxed on pay other than the statutory minimum wage and its holiday, overtime, night-shift and hazard pay.

references.title: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3): overtime and commissions are supplementary compensation, taxed with the period's regular pay on its column. The cumulative average method of s.2.79(B)(5)(a) is not computed: it divides by the count of payroll periods, which the balance does not hold, so the annualisation trues up the year.

RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(5)(b): cash basis. The year is read from `ctx.balances`, the tax year's checkpoint and scheme totals before this run, plus this run. A previous employer's Form 2316 figures count when `previous_employer_year` is this year or unrecorded. A last run paid in the next calendar year is not annualised here: the balance has closed, so the December run paid in December is the last one.
13th-month pay and other benefits are exempt to PHP90,000 in the aggregate
references.quote: Read 2026-11-04. 13th-month pay and other benefits are excluded from gross compensation up to PHP90,000 for the calendar year; the excess is taxable compensation. The pool holds ADDITIONAL_WAGES - ORDINARY_WAGES and each de minimis class's excess over its ceiling; the part already used this year is the same figures read from `ctx.balances.ytd`. Exempt termination pay and SSS benefits post at GROSS, which WTAX does not read, except for a non-resident alien not engaged in trade or business, taxed on all of it.

name: Fringe benefit tax

references.title: National Internal Revenue Code (as amended by RA 10963)
references.quote: Fringe benefits tax.

references.title: Revenue Regulations 11-2018
references.quote: A final tax of 35% on the grossed-up monetary value (÷ 65%) of fringe benefits granted to employees other than rank and file (25% ÷ 75% for a non-resident alien not engaged in trade or business), paid by the employer and not part of the employee's gross income; rank-and-file benefits are compensation. The monetary value is assigned by s.2.33(B) and RR 3-98.
